judgments.label: true_positive
judgments.rationale: The element is the 'Email address' input (type=email, name=loginEmail) of the sign-in form in the off-canvas account tray (app-tray-login), opened from the header's Account button. claimTrue: the snapshot's HTML for the input has no autocomplete attribute and its form (login-form) has none either; the label is 'Email address' and the field asks for the user's own login email, so the sentence holds. elementFails: the field collects information about the user and its purpose is in WCAG 2.1 section 7 (email); nothing identifies it programmatically. type=email is not enough: Understanding 1.3.5 says input types are 'only very broad categories, describing the type of input, but not necessarily its purpose', and H98 (autocomplete) is the sufficient technique. The tray being off-screen at capture does not take it out of scope: users open it and get this field. captureDiffers: the live HTML fetched with curl on 2026-11-25 has the same input with the same attributes and no autocomplete, and the rendered snapshot shows no script adding one; the screenshot is a styled render. The claim names exactly this failure, so true_positive.

judgments.label: true_positive
judgments.rationale: The element is the 'Password' input (type=password, name=loginPassword) of the same sign-in form in the account tray. claimTrue: the snapshot's HTML has no autocomplete attribute on the input or its form, and in a login form the field asks for the user's current password, so the sentence holds. elementFails: WCAG 2.1 section 7 lists 'current-password - The current password for the account identified by the username field (e.g., when logging in)' among the input purposes that relate to the user, so 1.3.5 applies, and without autocomplete=current-password (H98) the purpose is not programmatically determined; type=password gives only the broad type. captureDiffers: the live HTML fetched on 2026-11-25 has the same input without autocomplete (only the register form's password carries autocomplete=off, a different field), matching the snapshot. The claim names this failure, so true_positive.
